messages:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT CREATED — P1 — GeoDNS/External DNS failures affecting model-serving.api.redwood.com in us-west-2 and us-east-1. Symptoms: intermittent NXDOMAIN and 5xx from edge on ~30% of user resolvers. Automatic health-check failover triggered. Pages sent to on-call.

maya: saw the page, I'm on it. initial impact looks like failures for API traffic routed via Cloudflare + Route53 failover. hitting dig from my laptop shows inconsistent answers across resolvers. :eyes:

sam: jumping in — neteng. I can confirm from our monitoring that queries to the authoritative record are returning different sets of A records depending on resolver — some return the primary regional pool, others return nothing (NXDOMAIN). This smells like Route53 health check flapping + propagation combined with Cloudflare edge changes.

leo: tagging product/console — customer-facing errors: some websocket/connects failing and SDKs reporting 502/504. Need a severity assessment for customer comms.

chris: quick customer impact note: ~12% of requests across the hosted API are hitting error budget; Dedicated tenants with pinned IPs unaffected. We should assume broad read-only failures for clients using DNS-based routing.

maya: mitigation plan attempt 1: move to static failover by flipping Route53 record from latency-based to simple weighted with 100/0 to the secondary region to drain primary. Trying aws CLI now.

sam: before you flip, can you paste the dig traces? I'm seeing high TTL variance which will slow propagation. Also contacting Cloudflare support to ask about recently-deployed load-balancer rule.

maya: dig logs: ```
; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> +short model-serving.api.redwood.com @8.8.8.8
93.184.216.34

; <<>> DiG 9.16.1 <<>> +short model-serving.api.redwood.com @1.1.1.1
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached

; <<>> dig +trace model-serving.api.redwood.com
.  518400 IN NS a.root-servers.net.
...
```

ops-bot: Paging on-call: maya (primary), chris (backup) — acknowledge to proceed with mitigation. :bell:

maya: executing Route53 change: ```bash
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z12345 --change-batch file://failover-weighted-100.json
```

sam: I also ran `dig @ns-1.redwood-internal` — authoritative is returning mixed sets. Looks like one of our NS hosts in us-west-2 has intermittent network egress issues to Cloudflare, possibly an AZ-level routing flap. Opening ticket with infra to check BGP adjacencies.

cloudflare-support: Hi, Cloudflare here — we saw a recent LB rule rollout at 15:07 UTC that could cause some edge sessions to be marked unhealthy briefly. We're investigating and will share updates.

maya: Route53 change queued. Because of TTLs (~300s) this will take a few minutes to propagate; I'm also lowering TTL on the failover record to 60s to speed future flips. Executed: ```bash
aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --hosted-zone-id Z12345 --change-batch '{"Changes":[{"Action":"UPSERT","ResourceRecordSet":{"Name":"model-serving.api.redwood.com","Type":"A","TTL":60,"SetIdentifier":"us-west-2","Weight":100,"ResourceRecords":[{"Value":"93.184.216.34"}]}}]}'
```

chris: noted. meanwhile, enabling fallback at application layer for SDKs — return cached embeddings and degrade streaming to polling for affected endpoints. Pushing config to edge: `feature.flags.dns_fallback=true`.

sam: infra confirms a partial egress issue in us-west-2 AZ-b affecting our authoritative NS. They've rerouted BGP and cleared a problematic neighbor. Monitoring shows decreased NXDOMAIN counts.

ops-bot: Audit log: Route53 change recorded by maya at 2024-08-02T15:22:30Z.

maya: seeing improvement in edge errors — errors down from 30% to ~4% in last 2m. Still some stale caches returning NXDOMAIN.

cloudflare-support: update — rolled back LB rule at 15:25 UTC; that reduced edge unhealthiness. We also pushed an emergency config to prevent session resets, should be immediate.

leo: customer impact assessment draft: Affected: hosted API customers using default DNS-based routing in us-west-2/us-east-1. Estimated affected customers: ~85 active keys (small-medium apps), transient errors for others. No data loss. Action items: send short status update, include timeline and mitigation steps, offer extended logs on request.

maya: handoff to chris for monitoring and postmortem. chris, I'm going offline in 20m. Please confirm you have read the runbook and will follow up with RCA and comms.

chris: taking over. I've captured notes and flagged infra/neteng for RCA. Next steps: 1) full RCA draft within 48h, 2) TTL strategy review (we keep low TTL for failover records), 3) add automated probe across multiple public resolvers (8.8.8.8, 1.1.1.1, 9.9.9.9) to detect inconsistent authoritative answers.

sam: adding a permanent monitoring probe from multiple AZs and providers to detect authoritative divergence. Also will add a playbook step to pause LB rollouts during DNS health check windows.

maya: thanks team. I'm flagging this as resolved from primary on-call. Will add notes to incident tracker. :thumbsup:

incidents-bot: INCIDENT RESOLVED — P1 downgraded to P2 for postmortem/cleanup. Root cause: combination of Cloudflare LB rule causing transient edge unhealthiness + an AZ-level egress issue impacting one of our authoritative NS hosts leading to inconsistent DNS answers and health-check flapping in Route53.

chris: capturing the timeline in the incident doc and sending customer-facing update. Will link doc here when posted.

ops-bot: Incident timeline created: https://go.redwood/incident/2024-08-02-geo-dns-4821 (added to channels: incidents, eng-sre, product).

maya: final note — big props to sam and cloudflare-support for fast turnaround. :tada:

sam: good work all. we'll follow up on long-term fixes in the next infra retro. :eyes:
